stories.title: For Southern California, Defense Tech Is the Best Real Estate Offense
stories.excerpt: It’s easy to assume Los Angeles’ biggest contribution to the defense industry and any war effort has been the production of movies and films that celebrate the heroism of combat. But, due to persistent geopolitical instability, combat that’s draining crucial weapon stockpiles, and ongoing efforts to adapt the United States military to the modern demands of high-tech warfare, defense spending is skyrocketing. And no place is benefiting from that more than Southern California, especially the South Bay, a grouping of small cities adjacent to Los Angeles, including Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach and El Segundo, that have seen their port-adjacent warehouse spaces transformed into hubs of military manufacturing activity. “The growth curve we’re seeing for the South Bay right now is unprecedented,” said Mac Burridge, a managing director at JLL who leads the advanced manufacturing team. “It’s very akin to the Inland Empire during COVID, where there was just a frenzy for space and only a finite amount available.” Historically, the South Bay has been a hotbed of aeronautics and space technology. Many of the largest traditional defense contractors, known as the primes, operate out of Greater L.A., and SpaceX, which held its blockbuster initial public offering earlier this year, was incubated in the small city of El Segundo, a nexus of startups and innovation just south of Los Angeles International Airport. That tech activity has recently gone into overdrive, a mobilization that has become one of the bright spots of the Southern California economy. A record $366 billion was invested last year in California startups, driven by the AI boom. But the defense tech boom might be even more pronounced. Last summer’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act appropriated $153 billion in defense spending on top of record Pentagon budgets, with a proposed $1.5 trillion of spending for next year. bullets: Defense spending skyrocketing; South Bay (Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach, El Segundo) transformation underway.
Port-adjacent warehouse space converted to military manufacturing; growth compared to Inland Empire COVID surge.
JLL reports 'unprecedented growth curve' with finite available supply in LA South Bay submarket.
stories.summary: Southern California's South Bay—including Torrance, Hawthorne, Long Beach, and El Segundo—is experiencing unprecedented industrial demand driven by surging defense spending and high-tech military manufacturing. Port-adjacent warehouse spaces are being rapidly converted into defense production hubs. JLL's advanced manufacturing lead reports the growth mirrors the Inland Empire's COVID-era frenzy, with supply severely constrained.
stories.impact: Defense-driven industrialization will pull supply away from multifamily-zoned land and compress available industrial for adaptive reuse in LA South Bay. Developers should expect sharply rising industrial land values and tighter entitlements; conversely, defense payroll concentration may anchor long-term job/population growth in South Bay submarkets, sustaining rental demand if multifamily sites can be secured ahead of industrial land-grab. Flight to quality industrial will elevate construction costs and labor competition.

stories.title: SENTRE Acquires Carlsbad Industrial Long-Term Leased to Glanbia Nutritionals
stories.excerpt: CBRE facilitated the $26.6-million sale and financing of 2840 Loker Ave. East, a 104,298-square-foot industrial property in Carlsbad. CBRE’s Hunter Rowe, Michael Longo, Barbara Perrier and Matt Carlson represented the ownership, Bixby Capital Management and LaSalle Investment Management.. SENTRE purchased the property. The firm has completed more than $350 million in recent industrial investments across the Western U.S. CBRE’s Scott Peterson and Michael Kolcum secured financing for the buyer. Leasing advisory services were provided by CBRE’s Roger Carlson, Dennis Visser and Blake Wilson. The property is located within Carlsbad Technology Center and is 100% leased to Glanbia Nutritionals, a global nutrition and performance products company. The building has served as a key operational and logistics hub for Glanbia since 2001. “Investor demand and liquidity remain robust for mission-critical and advanced manufacturing industrial assets such as this one,” said Rowe. “The asset’s prime Carlsbad location, longstanding occupancy by Glanbia Nutritionals and strong underlying real estate fundamentals generated significant investor interest.” The post SENTRE Acquires Carlsbad Industrial Long-Term Leased to Glanbia Nutritionals appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SENTRE acquires $26.6M Carlsbad industrial; 104K SF, 100% leased to Glanbia Nutritionals since 2001.
Property in Carlsbad Technology Center; mission-critical logistics asset with longstanding occupancy.
Investor demand remains robust for advanced manufacturing and mission-critical industrial assets.
stories.summary: SENTRE purchased a 104,298-square-foot industrial building at 2840 Loker Ave. East in Carlsbad for $26.6 million. The property is fully leased to global nutrition company Glanbia Nutritionals and has served as its key logistics and operational hub since 2001. The sale signals strong investor appetite for mission-critical and advanced manufacturing industrial assets in prime Southern California locations.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, the Carlsbad Technology Center concentration of sticky, long-term industrial tenants and strong investor capital flowing to advanced manufacturing may reinforce industrial zoning protection in the submarket, reducing opportunities for residential conversion or mixed-use redevelopment in Carlsbad proper. Signals continued capital competition for West Coast industrial vs. residential.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges $277M Loan for Urby/Rockpoint JV on Jersey City Apartments
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged a $277-million construction loan on behalf of a joint venture between Urby and Rockpoint, for 201 Hudson – by Urby, a 748-unit multifamily development planned on the Jersey City waterfront. Co-Head of Global Debt & Structured Finance Jordan Roeschlaub and Vice Chairman Chris Kramer, Director Holden Witkoff and Analyst Jack Fenton arranged the financing with Truist. The financing will fund ongoing construction of the tower, which will feature a mix of studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom residences. The development will also include a pool, fitness center, social and coworking spaces, outdoor recreation areas and curated food-and-beverage offerings among its amenities. Located at 201 Hudson St. in Jersey City’s Paulus Hook neighborhood, 201 Hudson – by Urby represents the second phase of Urby’s waterfront residential development. Upon completion, the 69-story tower will deliver 748 market-rate apartments across approximately 528,000 rentable square feet, complemented by approximately 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space, extensive resident amenities and views of the Manhattan skyline and New York Harbor. The post Newmark Arranges $277M Loan for Urby/Rockpoint JV on Jersey City Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Urby/Rockpoint JV secures $277M construction loan from Truist for 748-unit Jersey City tower.
201 Hudson – by Urby; 69-story, 528K SF, Paulus Hook waterfront; mix of studios through 3-BR.
Second phase of Urby waterfront development; includes 10K SF retail, extensive amenities.
stories.summary: Urby and Rockpoint's joint venture obtained a $277 million construction loan from Truist to fund 201 Hudson – by Urby, a 748-unit, 69-story multifamily tower in Jersey City's Paulus Hook neighborhood. The project will deliver studio through three-bedroom market-rate apartments, ground-floor retail, and extensive amenities overlooking Manhattan and New York Harbor. This is the second phase of Urby's waterfront residential expansion.
stories.impact: Large-scale market-rate multifamily financing remains accessible in high-growth urban metros; Truist's commitment signals lender confidence in Jersey City waterfront demand and sponsorship strength. Paulus Hook's two-phase Urby buildout establishes anchor rental product in an already-competitive submarket, likely accelerating neighboring rents and land values. Developers eyeing Hudson County waterfront should expect increased competition for remaining entitled sites and potential rent-growth saturation by 2027–2028 delivery window.

stories.title: Pennrose Cuts Ribbon Second Phase of Providence Mixed-Income Rentals
stories.excerpt: Pennrose, the 195 District, the City of Providence, Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee, Mayor Brett Smiley, and project partners held the grand opening of Tandem, the second and final phase of the transformation of a 195 District parcel into a 127-unit mixed-use, mixed-income community. Tandem joins Tempo, which opened in April 2025, to complete the redevelopment of Parcel 9 with mixed-income housing, 1,100 square feet of ground floor retail, an affordable childcare facility and a public plaza. Tandem delivers 61 mixed-income, workforce, and market-rate rental homes. The building also includes eight one-bedroom-plus-den units, offering larger, more flexible layouts, along with one-bedroom and two-bedroom units with townhouse-style entrances off Bessie Way. “With Tandem now open, we’ve delivered on the full vision for Parcel 9,” said Karmen Cheung, regional VP at Pennrose. “This milestone reflects years of collaboration with incredible partners, including the195 District, the City of Providence, and RIHousing, whose shared commitment made this transformation possible.” The post Pennrose Cuts Ribbon Second Phase of Providence Mixed-Income Rentals appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pennrose opens Tandem, 61 units; completes 127-unit mixed-income Phase 2 in Providence Parcel 9.
Tempo (Phase 1) opened April 2025; combined project includes retail, childcare, public plaza.
Mixed-income, workforce, and market-rate units; public-private partnership with City and RIHousing.
stories.summary: Pennrose completed Tandem, the second phase of Parcel 9 redevelopment in Providence's 195 District, delivering 61 mixed-income, workforce, and market-rate rental units. Combined with Tempo (opened April 2025), the full project delivers 127 units across two buildings, plus ground-floor retail, an affordable childcare facility, and a public plaza. Development involved partnership with the City of Providence, RIHousing, and the 195 District.
stories.impact: Affordable and mixed-income pipeline moving steadily in Northeast secondary markets; Providence's 195 District redevelopment signals municipal willingness to support higher-density, mixed-income residential in urban cores. Developers should note strong availability of tax-credit and public-agency financing in Providence/Rhode Island; however, limited market-rate absorption may constrain future Phase 3+ returns, requiring careful underwriting of rent growth and income-mix feasibility in smaller metros.

stories.title: Hyatt Commercial Completes Office Lease in Maryland with Medical Practice
stories.excerpt: Hyatt Commercial announced that Menocal Family Practice has leased approximately 8,000 square feet at 1800 Dual Highway in Hagerstown, Maryland. Hyatt Commercial brokers Treva Ghattas and Laurie Murphy-Zuiderhof represented the landlord in leasing the space. The suite originally served as the executive offices of a financial institution. The transaction continues a growing trend of healthcare providers driving office leasing activity throughout Washington County. “We’re seeing healthcare providers become one of the primary drivers of leasing activity in Washington County. Buildings that can accommodate medical users—or be strategically converted—are significantly better positioned than those marketed solely to traditional office tenants,” said Treva Ghattas, Vice President at Hyatt Commercial. “We are excited to continue growing our practice at 1800 Dual Highway,” said Dr. Julio Menocal of Menocal Family Practice. “The new location provides the space and flexibility we need to serve more patients. It will also allow us to continue delivering the high-quality, personalized care our communities expect.” The post Hyatt Commercial Completes Office Lease in Maryland with Medical Practice appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Menocal Family Practice leases 8K SF at 1800 Dual Highway, Hagerstown, Maryland.
Healthcare providers emerging as primary office drivers in Washington County.
Formerly executive offices of financial institution; medical conversion accelerating trend.
stories.summary: Menocal Family Practice leased approximately 8,000 square feet at 1800 Dual Highway in Hagerstown, Maryland. The space was repurposed from a financial institution's executive offices. Brokers report healthcare providers are now the primary driver of office leasing activity throughout Washington County, positioning medical-compatible buildings as significantly more valuable than traditional office.
stories.impact: Secondary markets (Hagerstown/Washington County) are pivoting toward healthcare as last remaining office demand driver, pressuring traditional Class A office values. However, this signals rising medical/healthcare employment in smaller metros surrounding major MSAs—a potential source of workforce-housing demand. Multifamily developers in satellite markets should monitor healthcare employer expansion (clinics, urgent care, dental) as anchor tenancy for mixed-use or transit-adjacent apartment projects; Hagerstown's trend likely replicates in other suburban Rust Belt/Mid-Atlantic secondaries.

stories.title: Waterford Launches Construction on Milpitas Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Waterford Property Company has begun construction on a 75-unit affordable housing community in the Santa Clara County city of Milpitas. The project is being financed with 4% low-income tax credits and private activity bonds and is set for completion in early 2028. As part of a larger master planned community alongside new market-rate for-sale housing built by PulteGroup, Waterford’s new community is located at 1397 California Cir. and will target families with incomes between 30%, to70% of the Area Median Income. Through a partnership with nonprofit Pacific Housing, Inc, residents will have access to no-cost on-site social services programming. “We are extremely proud of our partnership with the City of Milpitas and PulteGroup to address the region’s need for more affordable housing. Waterford’s strength is working with local governments to deliver long-term, mission-aligned housing for vital community members. This includes teachers, nurses, first responders, and working families,” said Oren Hillel, Senior Director of development, Waterford Property Company. The post Waterford Launches Construction on Milpitas Affordable Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Waterford launches 75-unit affordable housing in Milpitas; 4% LIHTC, private activity bonds.
Target 30–70% AMI families; completion early 2028; part of larger PulteGroup master plan.
Partnership with Pacific Housing Inc for on-site social services; City of Milpitas subsidy/entitlements.
stories.summary: Waterford Property Company began construction on a 75-unit affordable housing community in Milpitas, California, financed with 4% low-income tax credits and private activity bonds. The project targets families earning 30–70% of area median income and will complete in early 2028. Residents will access no-cost social services through nonprofit Pacific Housing, Inc. The site sits within a larger master-planned community alongside PulteGroup market-rate for-sale homes.
stories.impact: Santa Clara County affordable pipeline remains active despite high land costs; mixed-income/affordable + for-sale master-plan strategy reflects local land constraint and inclusionary pressures. LIHTC availability and bond financing confirm strong subsidy market in high-cost CA metros. However, Milpitas' reliance on for-sale housing alongside affordable rental may limit market-rate rental absorption; multifamily developers should evaluate whether mixed-income rentals can compete with purchase options in Silicon Valley suburban submarkets, particularly if tech employment softens.

stories.title: Banyan Street, Independencia Refi South Florida Office With $54M
stories.excerpt: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management have nabbed $53.5 million to refinance an office complex in Doral, Fla. Wells Fargo provided the financing that backs the 290,000-square-foot Doral Center property. The 10.8-acre campus includes two buildings — one rising six stories and the other seven — at 3750 Northwest 87th Avenue and 8750 Northwest 36th Street in the Miami suburb. Doral Center, built between 1985 and 1990, is about 85 percent leased, according to CBRE, whose Amy Julian and Andrew Chilgren brokered the debt. Tenants include coworking operator Quest Workspaces, which leases about 38,000 square feet. The owners have spent $15.5 million updating the asset since buying it for $43 million in 2020 during the height of the pandemic. The 2020 sale price was about $4.3 million less than what the property had traded for four years earlier, according to property records. “The extensive capital improvements have completely transformed Doral Center into a premier workplace environment,” Julian said in a statement. “This strategic repositioning, combined with South Florida’s robust economic fundamentals, has enhanced the property’s competitiveness and triggered an immediate surge in leasing activity.” This January, the joint venture sold about three acres for $6 million to residential developer ROVR Development. A representative for Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Banyan Street/Independencia refinance $53.5M Doral Center office; 290K SF, 85% leased, Miami.
Wells Fargo financing; $15.5M capex since 2020 acquisition; coworking operator Quest Workspaces prime tenant.
Property repositioned; strategic updates to office product in Miami suburban market.
stories.summary: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management refinanced the 290,000-square-foot Doral Center in Doral, Florida for $53.5 million through Wells Fargo. The dual-building office campus, acquired in 2020 for $43 million, has been updated with $15.5 million in capital improvements and is 85% leased. Coworking operator Quest Workspaces is the largest tenant at ~38,000 square feet.
stories.impact: South Florida office repositioning (coworking, flex space) ongoing but at lower occupancy (85%) than pre-pandemic norms; refinancing signals lenders willing to back office stabilization in tier-2 metros, but cap rate/debt service compression indicates limited pricing power. Multifamily developers should note that Doral's office glut may free up secondary-market land/buildings for conversion or mixed-use redevelopment, but only at steep discounts; meanwhile, coworking demand suggests office-to-residential conversion risk remains real in Miami suburbs, creating competitive headwinds for new construction near Doral Center.

stories.title: Indian Restaurant Samudhra Takes 10K SF at 312 West 43rd Street
stories.excerpt: New Jersey-based Indian restaurant Samudhra is establishing a presence across the Hudson River in Hell’s Kitchen. The eatery signed a 10,000-square-foot lease on the ground level of the Ellery at 312 West 43rd Street, owned by Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors, for its second location in the U.S. following its first restaurant in Franklin Park, N.J., according to the landlords. Taconic did not disclose the asking rent or the length of the lease, but asking rent for prime retail space in the nearby Times Square retail corridor of Broadway and Seventh Avenue from 42nd to 47th streets was $1,400 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood,” George Tsapelas, senior vice president of Taconic, said in a statement. “From the outset, our vision for the Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area, and Samudhra further strengthens the retail and dining mix we’ve curated at the property.” CBRE’s Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh and Bevan Cohen negotiated on behalf of the landlord while Brad Schwarz from Lee & Associates handled the deal for the tenant. CBRE and Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The Ellery provides an exceptional setting for our New York City location and gives us the opportunity to introduce our distinctive premium Indian dining and lounge experience to a much broader audience,” Mangesh Chinthamaneni, founder and CEO at Samudhra, said in a statement. The announcement comes almost exactly a year after German grocery chain Aldi signed a lease spanning 25,000 square feet on the ground floor of the building in late August 2025 as part of Aldi’s broader rollout across the U.S. The New York Post first reported Samudhra’s lease deal. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Samudhra Indian restaurant leases 10K SF ground floor at 312 West 43rd Street, Hell's Kitchen, NYC.
Second U.S. location (first in Franklin Park, NJ); ground-level mixed-use in Taconic/NREA tower.
Times Square corridor prime retail $1,400/SF; strong restaurant/dining leasing activity in Midtown.
stories.summary: New Jersey-based restaurant Samudhra signed a 10,000-square-foot ground-floor lease at The Ellery (312 West 43rd Street) in Hell's Kitchen for its second U.S. location. The space was designed to support premium dining and social experience tenancy. Prime retail in the nearby Times Square corridor commands $1,400 per square foot, reflecting strong tenant demand.
stories.impact: Hell's Kitchen/West Midtown ground-floor retail pricing remains robust despite office distress; strong restaurant/dining demand supports mixed-use development fundamentals in Manhattan. However, high ground-floor rents ($1,400+/SF) compress returns on residential tower ground-floor space; developers should expect to hold or subsidize ground retail in new construction to achieve mixed-use feasibility in premium submarkets. 201 Hudson (Urby/Rockpoint) and similar waterfront towers should plan for restaurant/hospitality operators rather than traditional retail to justify rent.

stories.title: East Harlem Housing Proposal on City-Owned Lot Expands to 762 Units
stories.excerpt: An affordable and supportive housing complex slated for a city-owned site in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood just got 62 units larger. The New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) submitted plans on Friday to rezone the city block surrounding 22 East 119th Street. The requested amendments will facilitate a housing project spanning three buildings with a total of 762 units. PincusCo first reported on the filing. The site is currently occupied by a six-story, 174-unit single room occupancy building where Volunteers of America–Greater New York hosts supportive housing for formerly homeless, single adults, many of whom are veterans. In accordance with a city policy that avoids “spot zoning” individual tax lots, the rezoning proposal would impact the entire East Harlem block, bounded by East 118th and East 119th streets, between Madison and Fifth avenues. In addition to the site’s designation as an urban renewal area and the disposition of city-owned property, HPD’s requested amendments would label the block as a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area, ensuring affordable housing will be a part of any future redevelopments of the block’s privately owned buildings. A prior iteration of the project, sponsored by nonprofit Volunteers of America–Greater New York, planned 700 units across two buildings. Those included a 23-story supportive housing tower and a 25-story affordable housing tower. Plans also incorporated community space and commercial facilities for the nonprofit, with funding sought through HPD and the New York City Housing Development Corporation. Land use documents accompanying the newest proposal at 22 East 119th Street are not currently available. The change in site plans, and how surrounding buildings or project timelines will be impacted, is unclear. bullets: HPD rezones East Harlem block (E. 118–119, Madison–Fifth Ave) for 762-unit housing expansion.
Project grows from 174-unit existing SRO to 3-building, 762-unit affordable/supportive mix.
Replaces Volunteers of America single-room-occupancy facility; city policy avoids spot-zoning; urban renewal designation.
stories.summary: New York City's Department of Housing Preservation and Development filed rezoning for a block in Manhattan's East Harlem (22 East 119th Street) to facilitate a 762-unit affordable and supportive housing complex spanning three buildings. The proposal replaces a 174-unit SRO operated by Volunteers of America–Greater New York. Rezoning covers the entire block (E. 118–119 St., between Madison and Fifth Ave.) to comply with anti-spot-zoning policy.
stories.impact: Large-scale HPD disposition and rezoning signals aggressive public-sector multifamily pipeline acceleration in East Harlem; 762 units will compete directly with private market-rate and affordable development in Upper Manhattan, potentially suppressing rents and land values in the submarket through 2029–2030. Developers should expect East Harlem supply saturation and heightened affordability mandates/inclusionary requirements as spillover effect. Conversely, block-level rezoning may unlock additional development potential on neighboring parcels, creating extended pipeline risk for any mid-market or luxury projects in the corridor.

stories.title: Truist Lends $277M on Jersey City Multifamily Tower Build
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Rockpoint and Urby has secured $277 million of construction financing to develop the second phase of a multifamily tower in Jersey City, Commercial Observer has learned. Truist provided the loan for the sponsorship’s 748-unit 201 Hudson – by Urby project along the Jersey City waterfront. Rockpoint and Ubry joined forces to acquire land at 201 Hudson Street for the project in July, CO first reported at the time. “This financing reflects Truist’s continued commitment to supporting premier sponsors pursuing transformative multifamily developments in high-growth urban markets,” said Rebecca M. Cox, senior vice president and market manager at Truist National Real Estate. The transaction was led by Katie Kennedy, Northeast market leader at Truist, with Walt Reece, a director of real estate syndicated finance at Truist Securities, leading the syndication, according to the firm. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Chris Kramer, Holden Witkoff and Jack Fenton. The brokerage firm also advised the joint venture partners on the joint venture capitalization with a team composed of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Michael Collins. Located in Jersey City’s Paulus Hook neighborhood, 201 Hudson – by Urby marks the second phase of a 69-story tower that will include 528,000 rentable square feet and 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. Community amenities will include a pool, a fitness center and coworking spaces. Rockpoint, Urby and Newmark did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rockpoint/Urby JV secures $277M construction financing from Truist for 201 Hudson Jersey City.
748-unit Phase 2 tower; studio through 3-BR market-rate; 69-story waterfront development.
Financing reflects lender confidence in high-growth urban multifamily markets and premier sponsors.
stories.summary: Rockpoint and Urby's joint venture secured $277 million in construction financing from Truist for 201 Hudson – by Urby, a 748-unit multifamily tower in Jersey City's Paulus Hook waterfront. The 69-story development will deliver market-rate apartments ranging from studios to three-bedrooms, plus ground-floor retail and extensive amenities. Truist's backing underscores lender appetite for transformative multifamily in high-growth urban markets.
stories.impact: Construction lending remains accessible for large-scale market-rate multifamily in gateway metros and urban centers (Jersey City waterfront); Truist syndication support signals secondary lender participation and no material credit stress. Paulus Hook's rapid transformation (two-phase Urby buildout + additional planned residential) will establish strong rental comps, but delivery window (201 Hudson Phase 2 ~2027–2028) risks rent saturation if nearby Phase 1 (Tempo/Tandem-like competitors) deliver simultaneously. Developers with remaining Jersey City waterfront sites should accelerate acquisition and financing before land costs and construction caps fully reflect Urby-driven demand surge.
